ety.text: From ethic + -al, from Late Latin ethicus (“moral, ethical”), from Ancient Greek ἠθικός (ēthikós, “of or for morals, moral, expressing character”), from ἦθος (êthos, “character, moral nature”).

senses.d: Of or relating to the study of ethics.
ex: The philosopher Kant is particularly known for his ethical writings.

senses.d: Of or relating to the accepted principles of right and wrong, especially those of some organization or profession.
ex: All employees must familiarize themselves with our ethical guidelines.
We are trying to decide what the most ethical course of action would be.

senses.d: Only dispensed on the prescription of a physician.
ex: In most jurisdictions, morphine is classified as an ethical drug.

senses.d: An ethical drug, one only dispensed on the prescription of a physician.
